data.narrative:
Oxide Computer Company is a Series C-stage semiconductor company founded by Steve Tuck (CEO) and Bryan Cantrill (CTO). The valuation assessment draws from a comp universe of 3 public peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private companies in the chips and semiconductors sector, including Etched, d-Matrix, and DEEPX at the same stage.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses total capital raised ($389M) as a proxy base value and applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $661M. Peer-median methodology references three same-sector, same-stage comparables with a median valuation of $2.0B and a range spanning $529M (DEEPX floor) to $5.0B (Etched ceiling). The peer cohort exhibits material dispersion, reflecting varied technical positioning and funding momentum within the semiconductor frontier space.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $562M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.3B. The wide spread between stage-progression and peer-median results reflects two distinct signals: capital deployment history versus current market pricing of comparable-stage peers. Key uncertainties include the maturity of Oxide's product roadmap relative to Etched and d-Matrix, and whether the peer median appropriately anchors a company at Oxide's specific technical inflection point.
